encounter_greeting.text: Halt, ser {player}! I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I will not yield this road to any who would bar it. Stand aside or prove your mettle.
Good day, ser {player}. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction}. Our paths cross upon this road, so let us part with honour and without bloodshed, traveller.
Well met, friend {player}! {persona} of {my_faction} greets you. My ancestors would weep to see two honest parties pass without a word of cheer.

encounter_threatened.text: Pay {gold} to a man who has sworn an oath? Keep your coin, ser {player}. You shall have steel before you have a single piece of silver from me.
You name a price of {gold} and a surrender in one breath, ser {player}. I have kept my oath through worse threats than yours. Speak plainer, or step back.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for you would not cheapen yourself with a demand of {gold}. Let us speak again when the blood has cooled.
{gold} for my surrender? The Ouzmar hammer has been broken before and I still stand. Come and take what you want, ser {player}, and let the saga record your shame.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept your proposal, ser {player}. Our banners shall stand together against {enemy_faction}, and my hammer will answer for the oath we swear.
By my oath, ser {player}, I accept! We shall break {enemy_faction} together, and the saga will name us allies in arms for generations.
Agreed, ser {player}. I will not share a fire with {rival}, but you I trust. Let us march against {enemy_faction} and let our word be the bond between us.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I must decline, ser {player}. An alliance is an oath, and I do not swear lightly. Perhaps when the moon is kinder we may speak of it again.
No, ser {player}. I will not bind my hammer to yours while you keep company with {rival}. Prove your honour first, and then we shall talk.
I regret I must refuse, ser {player}. Your offer is honourable, but my vow forbids it for now. Know that I remember your courtesy all the same.

captured_by_player.text: Bound and beaten, yet not broken, ser {player}. Ask your ransom of {my_faction} if you must, but know that I will not beg before you.
I am your captive, ser {player}, and I will not dispute it. {gold} is what you ask, and {my_faction} will pay it in time, for our oaths bind us to one another.
A fine stroke brought me low, ser {player}. You have my respect, and I shall tell my kin that you fought as an honest knight and held your captive with fairness.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have ransomed me and did not. I shall not forget this mercy, and my hammer owes you a debt.
Let it be known that ser {player} released me without ransom. Mercy such as that is rare on these roads, and my hammer honours it.
You loosed my chains, ser {player}, and asked nothing of me. I cannot yet call us friends, but I will not forget the mercy shown.
Ser {player} let me go rather than take my coin. I still count you a rival to my faction, but I will not deny the mercy you showed.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction} like a coward turning from the field. Let the saga record this betrayal.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Oaths are hard to keep and easy to break, so I shall judge by what you do next.
I grieve to see you leave {my_faction}, ser {player}, though I will not curse you. Your honour is still yours to keep, wherever you march.

war_declared.text: Upon my hammer's oath, {my_faction} takes up arms against {enemy_faction}! Let the saga remember which banners marched first.
Let the bells of {my_faction} ring out! War is declared on {enemy_faction}, and I shall stand in the first rank as my ancestors did.
{enemy_faction} has thrown down the gauntlet to {my_faction}. Very well, I accept it, and I shall answer with my hammer and my name.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, your shield stood beside mine at the ford. With {troop_count} blades we broke {enemy_faction}. I shall not forget it, friend.
Ser {player}, we fought as one with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction}, and not a man turned from the line. Such courage honours us both, traveller.

encounter_farewell.text: We part for now, ser {player}, but I shall not forget your face. When next we meet, let the hammer speak for us both.
Go well on your road, ser {player}. May your oaths be kept and your banners held high until we meet again.
Farewell, friend {player}. Walk in honour, and I shall walk in honour too. Until the roads cross again, my hand is open to you.
Begone for now, ser {player}. Our quarrel is not finished, and the saga shall not close until it is settled between us.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} is a fine omen for the smithies. A good hammer rings truest on a wet morning, friends.
Word from {village} is that the bread is thin this season. Still, the folk there keep their oaths, and I honour them for it.
Stalwart folk of {town}, keep your oaths and your forges burning. The saga is long and the road is longer still.
Someone in {village} called the road a grind. A grind? Speak of honest labour, not of such words, I beg you.
Tools sent to {town} under oath must be carried with care, for no lazy hand should touch a vow made in iron.
